=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law

## Preliminary point: the Seller's "FINAL" framing

The Seller's preamble makes two claims. First, it says these positions are "market standard." Second, it says they were "settled at principal level," are "FINAL," and are "not intended to be re-opened." Both are negotiating assertions in the other side's draft. They do not bind us and I have not treated them as constraints.

**Action:** Before marking up, confirm with Wattlebridge's principals whether anything was actually agreed, and on what terms. If nothing was agreed, every point below is open.

The disclosures themselves also undercut the "FINAL" claim. They admit that Bluefen consent is not obtained, Riverlark is not repaid, Ironquay IP has not transferred, the bonuses are outside the funds flow, and the privacy incident is unresolved.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m). The Seller seeks to apply it to all Claims (see N-004, N-005 and N-014).
- **Buyer wants:** An opening counter of 30–40%. The cap should apply **only** to general warranty claims. Fundamental, tax, specific indemnity, covenant and fraud claims should sit outside it.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at a higher figure. Trade down to 20% only if every carve-out sits outside the cap. *Reason: 20% is tolerable only if the known, quantified exposures (Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, privacy) are not competing for the same AUD 4.8m.* If W&I insurance is in play, revisit this point together with the policy limit and retention.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis of AUD 25,000 per claim. Basket of AUD 250,000 (about 1.04% of price), with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis of AUD 10,000–15,000, with related claims aggregated. Basket of about AUD 120,000 (0.5%). The basket should be a **tipping basket**, so the first dollar is recoverable once it is exceeded. Neither threshold should apply to fundamental, tax, indemnity or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the deductible structure and counter as above. *Reason: a deductible plus a high de minimis could leave several hundred thousand dollars of real loss permanently unrecoverable.* Note the risk for the Sandbar renewals: three claims of AUD 110,000 each could each be argued separately.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion. The Seller also proposes that this limit applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general warranties, so that at least one full audit cycle under Buyer ownership is covered. Longer, separate periods should apply to other categories (see N-004, N-014 and N-016).
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months and reject the "applies to all Claims" default. *Reason: 18 months may not cover a full post-Completion audit, and the default would silently shorten tax and title claims.*

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties would be subject to the same cap and time limit as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (capacity, authority, title, no encumbrances, capital structure) capped at 100% of price, with no de minimis or basket, and a time limit of at least 6 years (aligned with the NSW contract limitation period).
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: if title fails, we have paid AUD 24m for shares we do not own, so a AUD 4.8m cap and an 18-month limit is not "simplicity" but an 80% haircut on the core bargain.*

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions to "all Claims of any nature." There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out. None of the limitations, the exclusive-remedy clause or the non-reliance clause should apply to fraud, wilful misconduct or wilful concealment by the Seller, the Company or their officers or advisers. Claims of that kind should be uncapped and not time-limited.
- **Recommendation:** This is a must-have, and our position should be non-negotiable. *Reason: no buyer should contractually release the Seller from its own fraud, and the drafting as it stands arguably attempts exactly that.*

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 and everything else in it), the Accounts, the statutory registers and all public records. In addition, paragraph 1.4 states that nothing in the letter admits breach.
- **Buyer wants:** Only **fair and specific** disclosure against identified warranties, with enough detail for the Buyer to assess the nature and scope of each matter. The Buyer would accept, at most, a limited deemed disclosure of the data room index and of specified searches run on a stated date. There should be no general disclosure of the data room or of "publicly searchable records."
- **Recommendation:** Reject paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2 in their current form and insert a fair-disclosure standard. *Reason: blanket disclosure turns the warranties into a reverse due-diligence exercise and could neutralise claims for every issue listed in this memo.* Also confirm that paragraph 1.4 cannot be read to cut down specific indemnities.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 would bar any claim about a matter known to the Buyer **or its advisers**, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Ideally a pro-sandbagging clause, or at least silence on the point. The fallback is that only the *actual* knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals counts, with no constructive or adviser knowledge. Specific indemnities and fundamental warranties must be expressly excluded from any knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: combined with general disclosure, clause 8.3 would bar claims on every known issue, including the ones we are pricing through specific indemnities.*

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** The Seller would use "reasonable endeavours," and the condition would be treated as satisfied on delivery of a written consent. However, Disclosure Letter item 2 confirms that **no consent has been obtained and the clause 11.3 conditions are not shown to be satisfied**. Bluefen represents about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A condition precedent (CP) for the Buyer's benefit requiring written, unconditional and irrevocable Bluefen consent in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, with all clause 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived by Bluefen.
  - Satisfaction determined by the Buyer, not deemed.
  - Only the Buyer may waive the CP.
  - A long-stop date with a walk right.
  - Pre-Completion covenants giving the Buyer visibility of all correspondence with Bluefen.
- **Recommendation:** Reject deemed satisfaction and insist on the Buyer-controlled CP. *Reason: a conditional or defective consent from a 30% customer goes to valuation, and "reasonable endeavours" puts the risk on us.* Consider a price adjustment or earn-out protection if the consent comes with commercial conditions attached.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release to be provided **after** Completion. About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, not repaid, and no discharge has been delivered. The facility contains a change-of-control clause (8.1).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A payoff letter from Riverlark Bank before Completion, confirming the exact payout amount and an undertaking to release.
  - Repayment at Completion out of the purchase price, as an itemised Indebtedness deduction in the funds flow.
  - Delivery at Completion of a deed of release and discharge, PPSR financing statement releases, and returned security documents.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release. *Reason: on a debt-free/cash-free deal we must not pay the full price, take a company that carries AUD 3.2m of secured debt, and then rely on the Seller to clear it.* Also confirm that signing does not trigger a default under clause 8.1 in the meantime.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000 (DD-005) are "a matter for the Seller," yet they do **not** appear in the funds flow. On-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The bonuses, plus all associated payroll tax, superannuation (where applicable), PAYG withholding and workers' compensation on-costs, treated as Transaction Costs or Indebtedness and deducted from the price.
  - Payment through Company payroll at Completion, funded by the Seller.
  - A specific indemnity, outside the cap and basket, covering any shortfall, on-costs or employee claims.
- **Recommendation:** Itemise the bonuses in the funds flow as a price deduction. *Reason: the Company is the employer, so unless they are deducted, the Buyer economically funds AUD 420,000 plus on-costs that the Seller says are "its matter."*

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity in clause 11.1 covers only the SOW3 payment. Under DD-004 clause 7.3, ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials passes only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, and there is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A completion deliverable or CP: evidence of cleared payment (or payment at Completion out of Seller proceeds) **and** an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, including moral rights consents.
  - A broadened indemnity covering any loss arising from the Company not owning SOW3 materials or any Ironquay claim, including infringement, re-development cost and loss of revenue.
  - The indemnity to sit outside the cap and basket, with a time limit of at least 4–6 years.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the indemnity as "adequate." *Reason: the risk is not the AUD 180,000 but that the Company may not own core product IP, which a payment-only indemnity does not address.*

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** Described as a "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material. Disclosure Letter item 6 records a download link sent to an unintended external address, potentially covering about 1,240 records. Access, scope and notification obligations are all unresolved, and the investigation is still preliminary.
- **Timing concern:** The incident was known by 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026. The 30-day period for assessing whether an eligible data breach has occurred under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), Part IIIC) has likely **already expired**. Whether the Company has complied is itself a live issue.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Immediate information: the forensic findings, the NDB assessment, any notification made to the OAIC or to affected individuals, and whether the link was accessed.
  - Pre-Completion covenants requiring the investigation to be completed and any notifications made in consultation with the Buyer.
  - Specific privacy and data-protection warranties.
  - A specific indemnity, outside the cap, basket and knowledge qualifier, covering regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, and third-party claims (including under the new statutory privacy tort).
  - Consideration of a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Treat this as a specific-indemnity item, not a disclosed-away matter. *Reason: the exposure is unquantified, regulator-facing, and possibly already compounded by a missed assessment deadline.*

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 in total) are said to be ordinary-course costs. Disclosure Letter item 8 itself says they should be "read together for timing/scope" and does not confirm that they are ordinary course, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Copies of all three contracts, with signing dates and the approvals given.
  - Confirmation of whether the renewals were deliberately split to stay below an approval or conduct-of-business threshold.
  - Aggregation for all thresholds.
  - Any amount accrued or prepaid and unpaid at Completion treated as a debt-like item.
  - If the renewals are not genuinely ordinary course, unwind or termination rights, or a price adjustment or specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" characterisation until diligence confirms it. *Reason: three identical related renewals, flagged for joint reading, look like threshold-splitting until shown otherwise.*

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." Combined with clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5, this collapses every category into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** An express liability table that separates each category, with limitations applying only where stated:

| Category | Cap | Thresholds | Time limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| General warranties | Per N-001 | Per N-002 | 24 months |
| Fundamental | 100% of price | None | 6+ years |
| Tax | 100% of price | None | Statutory period + 6 months (or 5–7 years) |
| Specific indemnities | Outside general cap (100% of price or specific caps) | None | 4–6 years |
| Covenants / leakage | As agreed | None | As agreed |
| Fraud | Uncapped | None | None |

- **Recommendation:** Reject the default and replace it with the table. *Reason: the default is the single drafting mechanism through which the Seller's other positions quietly strip the value of every carve-out.*

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the Company's own share register (DD-012). Disclosure Letter item 10 concedes this is not Buyer verification.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Independent checks: an ASIC company extract and historical search, review of the constitution and share issue history (allotment documents and transfer records), confirmation that no options, convertibles, ESOP awards or other rights over shares exist, and a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company.
  - Completion deliverables: executed share transfers, share certificates (or a lost-certificate indemnity), board approval of the transfer and register update, releases of any encumbrances, and director resignations.
  - Title treated as a fundamental warranty (see N-004).
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the register alone. *Reason: the register is the Seller's own document, and title is the one thing the AUD 24m buys.*

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime," meaning a 20% cap, the basket and 18 months.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** A standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion taxes, including payroll tax and superannuation on the bonuses and any shortfall interest or penalties. Full tax warranties. Buyer control of pre-Completion returns with Seller review. Outside the cap and basket, with a time limit of the statutory amendment period plus 6 months.
  - **IP:** Full IP warranties covering ownership, chain of title (Ironquay, employee and contractor assignments), open-source use, non-infringement and moral rights. Time limit of 3–4 years, with a higher cap or treatment as quasi-fundamental for core product IP.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled." *Reason: tax and IP are the two areas where loss typically surfaces after 18 months, and IP here already has a known defect (Ironquay).*

---

## Priority summary

**Walk-away level (must-haves):**
- N-005: fraud carve-out
- N-004 and N-015: fundamental warranties and title
- N-009: Riverlark repaid at Completion
- N-008: Bluefen consent as a Buyer-controlled CP
- N-014: category separation

**Price or indemnity items:**
- N-010: bonuses plus on-costs (AUD 420,000+)
- N-011: Ironquay IP
- N-012: privacy incident
- N-013: Sandbar renewals

**Tradeable:**
- N-001: cap
- N-002: thresholds
- N-003: time limit
- N-007 fallback wording on buyer knowledge (only after the carve-outs are secured)

**Immediate diligence requests:**
- Bluefen correspondence and clause 11.3 status
- Riverlark payoff figure
- Ironquay payment records
- Privacy incident forensic report and NDB assessment
- The three Sandbar contracts
- ASIC and PPSR searches

*Caveat: this memo is based solely on the Seller's summary and disclosure letter. The full SPA text should be checked against each point, and the specific statutory and tax references should be confirmed by the relevant specialists before the mark-up goes out.*

- **Recommendation:** Reject deemed satisfaction and insist on the Buyer-controlled CP. *Reason: a conditional or defective consent from a 30% customer goes to valuation, and "reasonable endeavours" puts the risk on us.* Consider a price adjustment or earn-out protection if the consent comes with commercial conditions attached.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release to be provided **after** Completion. About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, not repaid, and no discharge has been delivered. The facility contains a change-of-control clause (8.1).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A payoff letter from Riverlark Bank before Completion, confirming the exact payout amount and an undertaking to release.
  - Repayment at Completion out of the purchase price, as an itemised Indebtedness deduction in the funds flow.
  - Delivery at Completion of a deed of release and discharge, PPSR financing statement releases, and returned security documents.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release. *Reason: on a debt-free/cash-free deal we must not pay the full price, take a company that carries AUD 3.2m of secured debt, and then rely on the Seller to clear it.* Also confirm that signing does not trigger a default under clause 8.1 in the meantime.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000 (DD-005) are "a matter for the Seller," yet they do **not** appear in the funds flow. On-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The bonuses, plus all associated payroll tax, superannuation (where applicable), PAYG withholding and workers' compensation on-costs, treated as Transaction Costs or Indebtedness and deducted from the price.
  - Payment through Company payroll at Completion, funded by the Seller.
  - A specific indemnity, outside the cap and basket, covering any shortfall, on-costs or employee claims.
- **Recommendation:** Itemise the bonuses in the funds flow as a price deduction. *Reason: the Company is the employer, so unless they are deducted, the Buyer economically funds AUD 420,000 plus on-costs that the Seller says are "its matter."*

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity in clause 11.1 covers only the SOW3 payment. Under DD-004 clause 7.3, ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials passes only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, and there is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A completion deliverable or CP: evidence of cleared payment (or payment at Completion out of Seller proceeds) **and** an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, including moral rights consents.
  - A broadened indemnity covering any loss arising from the Company not owning SOW3 materials or any Ironquay claim, including infringement, re-development cost and loss of revenue.
  - The indemnity to sit outside the cap and basket, with a time limit of at least 4–6 years.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the indemnity as "adequate." *Reason: the risk is not the AUD 180,000 but that the Company may not own core product IP, which a payment-only indemnity does not address.*

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** Described as a "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material. Disclosure Letter item 6 records a download link sent to an unintended external address, potentially covering about 1,240 records. Access, scope and notification obligations are all unresolved, and the investigation is still preliminary.
- **Timing concern:** The incident was known by 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026. The 30-day period for assessing whether an eligible data breach has occurred under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), Part IIIC) has likely **already expired**. Whether the Company has complied is itself a live issue.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Immediate information: the forensic findings, the NDB assessment, any notification made to the OAIC or to affected individuals, and whether the link was accessed.
  - Pre-Completion covenants requiring the investigation to be completed and any notifications made in consultation with the Buyer.
  - Specific privacy and data-protection warranties.
  - A specific indemnity, outside the cap, basket and knowledge qualifier, covering regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, and third-party claims (including under the new statutory privacy tort).
  - Consideration of a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Treat this as a specific-indemnity item, not a disclosed-away matter. *Reason: the exposure is unquantified, regulator-facing, and possibly already compounded by a missed assessment deadline.*

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 in total) are said to be ordinary-course costs. Disclosure Letter item 8 itself says they should be "read together for timing/scope" and does not confirm that they are ordinary course, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Copies of all three contracts, with signing dates and the approvals given.
  - Confirmation of whether the renewals were deliberately split to stay below an approval or conduct-of-business threshold.
  - Aggregation for all thresholds.
  - Any amount accrued or prepaid and unpaid at Completion treated as a debt-like item.
  - If the renewals are not genuinely ordinary course, unwind or termination rights, or a price adjustment or specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" characterisation until diligence confirms it. *Reason: three identical related renewals, flagged for joint reading, look like threshold-splitting until shown otherwise.*

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." Combined with clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5, this collapses every category into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** An express liability table that separates each category, with limitations applying only where stated:

| Category | Cap | Thresholds | Time limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| General warranties | Per N-001 | Per N-002 | 24 months |
| Fundamental | 100% of price | None | 6+ years |
| Tax | 100% of price | None | Statutory period + 6 months (or 5–7 years) |
| Specific indemnities | Outside general cap (100% of price or specific caps) | None | 4–6 years |
| Covenants / leakage | As agreed | None | As agreed |
| Fraud | Uncapped | None | None |

- **Recommendation:** Reject the default and replace it with the table. *Reason: the default is the single drafting mechanism through which the Seller's other positions quietly strip the value of every carve-out.*

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the Company's own share register (DD-012). Disclosure Letter item 10 concedes this is not Buyer verification.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Independent checks: an ASIC company extract and historical search, review of the constitution and share issue history (allotment documents and transfer records), confirmation that no options, convertibles, ESOP awards or other rights over shares exist, and a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company.
  - Completion deliverables: executed share transfers, share certificates (or a lost-certificate indemnity), board approval of the transfer and register update, releases of any encumbrances, and director resignations.
  - Title treated as a fundamental warranty (see N-004).
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the register alone. *Reason: the register is the Seller's own document, and title is the one thing the AUD 24m buys.*

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime," meaning a 20% cap, the basket and 18 months.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** A standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion taxes, including payroll tax and superannuation on the bonuses and any shortfall interest or penalties. Full tax warranties. Buyer control of pre-Completion returns with Seller review. Outside the cap and basket, with a time limit of the statutory amendment period plus 6 months.
  - **IP:** Full IP warranties covering ownership, chain of title (Ironquay, employee and contractor assignments), open-source use, non-infringement and moral rights. Time limit of 3–4 years, with a higher cap or treatment as quasi-fundamental for core product IP.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled." *Reason: tax and IP are the two areas where loss typically surfaces after 18 months, and IP here already has a known defect (Ironquay).*
